summary: Patrol lookout since 1915, a D-6 cupola in the 1920s, then the present 1948 L-4 cab on Drake Peak, now the highest road-accessible lookout in Oregon and a Recreation.gov rental.

access.note: Rentable via Recreation.gov; combination lock code provided on booking.

visit.trail_note: Road access to the summit; highest road-accessible lookout in Oregon per NHLR.

events.note: First used as a patrol lookout; fire-finding instruments installed.
Standard Forest Service road built to the site.
D-6 cupola built on Drake Peak per NHLR; firelookout.com instead places a D-6 cupola cabin on nearby Light Peak in 1926 -- sources disagree on location and year.
Present L-4 ground house built new next to the cupola, cost $3,451.47.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register March 31, 2003.

evidence.supports: Patrol lookout since 1915 with fire-finding instruments
evidence.quote: Drake's Peak was first used as a patrol lookout and had fire-finding instruments installed in 1915.
In the summer of 1927 a standard Forest Service road was constructed next to the summit.
A D-6 cupola was built there in 1928.

evidence.supports: D-6 cupola cabin built 1926 on Light Peak, half mile northeast
evidence.quote: A D-6 cupola cabin was built atop Light Peak 1/2 mile to the northeast in 1926.
The present L-4 ground house was constructed, brand new, next to the cupola in 1948 at a cost of $3451.47.
Drake Peak (elev. 8352') has the distinction of being the highest lookout with road access in Oregon.
The biggest excitement at Drake Mountain Lookout on the Fremont National Forest comes when lightning strikes the adjacent propane tank.

evidence.supports: Forest Service personnel staffed through fire seasons, watching for lightning, flames, smoke
evidence.quote: Historically, Forest Service personnel lived long seasons in the cabin, scanning the region for lightning, flames, curls of smoke or any other indicator of possible forest fires.

evidence.supports: Sleeps up to four, folding cots, wood stove
evidence.quote: The small, 14 x 14-foot lookout is designed to accommodate up to four people and is furnished with folding cots, a table and chairs, a wood stove for heat

evidence.supports: No water on site, water available 6 miles away at Mud Creek Campground
evidence.quote: Guests may fill water jugs at Mud Creek Campground approximately 6 miles away.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates a D-6 cupola on Drake Peak itself to 1928; firelookout.com instead dates a D-6 cupola cabin on neighboring Light Peak to 1926. The story notes this disagreement rather than picking one.

notes_for_editor: Brief's conflict note ('they share a register number') appears to be a brief-generation artifact, not addressed here since no evidence was found that Drake Peak and Bald Butte actually share an NHLR number; NHLR page for Drake Peak gives its own distinct register entry. Flagging for editor to check the queue tool's register-number field if this matters.
